{{short description|Canadian physicist and astronomer|bot=PearBOT 5}}
'''Norbert Bartel''' is a Canadian [[physicist]] and [[astronomer]], currently a Distinguished Research Professor at [[York University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=http://www.yorku.ca/bartel/ |title=Norbert Bartel |publisher=yorku.ca |accessdate=January 29, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n85015379/ |title=Bartel, Norbert |publisher=worldcat.org |accessdate=January 29, 2017}}</ref>

== Education ==
Studying in Germany, Bartel received a [[Diplom|Vordiplom]] in Physics from [[University of Hamburg]] in 1972 and  a  M.Sc. [[Diplom]] in Physics from the [[University of Bonn]], in 1975. He received a PhD in Physics and Astronomy from the University of Bonn and the [[Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy]] in 1978.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.yorku.ca/bartel/CV.html|title=Curriculum Vitae|last=Bartel|first=Norbert|website=www.yorku.ca|access-date=2018-10-19}}</ref>

== Career ==
From 1983 until 1992 Bartel was a research associate at the [[Harvard–Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics|Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics]]. In 1992, he joined the faculty of the York University Department of Physics and Astronomy.<ref name=":0" />

His research involves using [[very-long-baseline interferometry]] (VLBI) radio astronomy to study the structure and evolution of [[Supernova remnant|supernova remnants]], [[Pulsar wind nebula|pulsar wind nebulae]] and [[Active galactic nucleus|active galactic nuclei]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nrao.edu/pr/2004/sn1986j/|title=Radio Telescopes Reveal Youngest Stellar Corpse|website=www.nrao.edu|access-date=2018-10-19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.universetoday.com/9652/youngest-black-hole-found/?162004|title=Youngest Black Hole Found? - Universe Today|date=2004-06-11|work=Universe Today|access-date=2018-10-19|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
In 1978, Bartel received the Max Planck Society [[Otto Hahn Medal]]. In 2006, he was appointed a Distinguished Research Professor at York University.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://vpap.info.yorku.ca/awards-and-recognition/distinguished-research-professors/|title=Distinguished Research Professors {{!}} Provost & Vice-President Academic|website=vpap.info.yorku.ca|language=en-US|access-date=2018-10-19}}</ref>
